transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-22
Start time: 16:30 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Marcus (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SA), Priya (CISO - Hearthwell), David (Head of Infra), Liam (Cloud Architect), Maya (Compliance), Samir (DevOps)

Summary: High-level security architecture deep dive focused on private deployment (VPC/on-prem), egress/ingress hardening, KMS integration and audit log retention for SOC 2/ISO readiness. Customer has strict egress controls and regulatory residency constraints. Discussed airlock pattern, outbound-only proxies, HSM/KMS trust model, RBAC/SSO mapping, and log forwarding. Agreed next steps and action items.

Topics: Network segmentation, egress proxies, egress allow-lists vs deny-first, KMS key wrapping and HSM options, audit log pipelines, RBAC and SSO integration (SCIM/SAML), data residency and encryption at rest, SOC 2 evidence mapping.

[00:00] Marcus: all right let's kick off thanks everyone for joining, um today the goal is to run through a security-first design for the private deployment and nail down egress + kms questions we promised priya and team.
[00:12] Priya: thanks Marcus, yes we need a concrete audit path for SOC two and ISO 27001 and we need to understand what evidence we'll get from Redwood if we host private.
[00:20] Marcus: yep, totally. Sofia will run through the recommended architecture and then ravi will surface the KMS options and audit log flows.
[00:26] Sofia: hi all, quick note, i'll share the diagram in the chat after the call, it's under redwood/arch/hearthwell-airlock-2026 link.
[00:34] (link posted) https://redwood.app/arch/hearthwell-airlock-2026
[00:38] David: quick context — we run a hybrid setup: core claims platform on-prem in two DCs, new ML inference workloads are planned in a private VPC in AWS but must not egress to the public internet except through approved proxies. we also have a vendor lockdown policy for external network flows.
[00:52] Sofia: understood. recommended pattern is an airlock egress gateway with TLS termination inside your VPC, mutual TLS to Redwood peering, and optional private link — we support both private link and site-to-site VPN.
[01:05] Priya: do you support customer-managed KMS in the private deployment, i mean actual HSM or BYOK so keys never leave our control?
[01:13] Ravi: yes, we support customer-managed keys. you can either bring your own KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) with key policies that we can be granted access to for encryption/decryption via service identities, or use an HSM-backed KMS where the key never leaves the HSM. we can integrate using envelope encryption.
[01:29] Liam: can you walk through the handshake — i want to understand how Redwood fetches model blobs and whether those blobs transit our egress or are pulled by Redwood into its private pool?
[01:38] Marcus: good question. there are two patterns — for private deployments you can either let Redwood host model artifacts in a managed model registry accessible over a VPC peering/private link, or you can stage artifacts in your S3 and Redwood pulls them over a presigned, time-limited transfer initiated from your VPC. if you want zero egress you can mirror model artifacts into an internal artifact store and provide Redwood with in-situ access via a bastion or courier process.
[01:58] David: slightly concerned about presigned urls — that pattern often requires temporary public endpoints. can we ensure the presigned transfer is only over the private link?
[02:07] Sofia: yes the presigned URL approach is optional; if you peer via private link then the entire transfer never leaves private network. presigned is only for convenience when private connectivity isn't available.
[02:14] Priya: on logs — SOC 2 will require immutable audit trails. how do we get tamper-evident logs for inference requests and admin actions?
[02:22] Ravi: we stream structured audit events to your log collector (syslog/fluentd/stackdriver) with signed event envelopes. for extra guarantee you can route a copy to your write-once storage or to a remote SIEM with write-once retention. we also offer an optional signed-hash chain for key lifecycle events.
[02:36] Maya: what about PII redaction in logs — we cannot send raw prompts off-prem if they include sensitive fields.
[02:42] Sofia: we advise prefix-level redaction and a local preprocessor that masks PII before it's included in logs. in private deploy you can run the preprocessor inside your VPC so nothing sensitive leaves.
[02:52] Samir: for egress firewall rules, do you have a minimal allow-list? our security team likes deny-first so we need explicit host + port lists.
[02:59] Marcus: yes we've published minimal egress requirements — mainly to Redwood control plane IPs, container registry endpoints, and optional telemetry endpoints. but for private deployment telemetry is optional — you can disable telemetry or route it to a customer-managed endpoint.
[03:13] (Sofia posts snippet of allowed-ips.txt)
[03:16] Sofia: note these are example ranges; for a hardened setup we recommend you only allow the peering CIDR and our orchestration endpoint plus any artifact mirror.
[03:28] Priya: if we use mutual TLS and a proxy, how is the cert lifecycle managed? we cannot have long-lived certs that are unmanaged.
[03:36] Ravi: we support automated cert rotation via ACME for edge proxies, and for mTLS between nodes we recommend short-lived service certs minted by your internal CA or by Vault. Redwood can integrate with your cert-issuing pipeline to accept rotated certs automatically.
[03:49] Liam: does the Redwood runtime require outbound DNS resolution to the public internet?
[03:55] Sofia: only if you use vendor hosted endpoints. in private mode you can control DNS and provide private hosted zones for registry endpoints; no public DNS needed.
[04:03] (15-second pause, typing / background noise)
[04:20] Priya: a compliance question — for SOC 2 we need user access logs for administrative actions with SSO mapping, can Redwood forward admin events to our audit system and map SAML principals to Redwoods RBAC?
[04:31] Marcus: yes. we map SAML/SCIM attributes into our RBAC layer. we can emit admin events with the SAML subject and we also persist the mapped role and raw assertion metadata for traceability.
[04:43] Maya: will that raw assertion include email addresses? we need to make sure PHI rules don't leak identities in some contexts.
[04:50] Sofia: we can redact the assertion or only emit a UUID-mapped subject. that mapping lives in your vault so only you can reconcile identity to email.
[04:58] David: what about egress latency — we measured previous vendors adding a 80–120ms tail when routing via an external proxy, will your runtime add similar overhead?
[05:08] Ravi: there is some overhead for TLS termination and proxying; with private link and colocated endpoints we've seen sub-20ms median extra latency for token generation and model ops, worst-case tail depends on network path. our recommendation is colocating a small inference pool in your region and use local peering.
[05:23] Liam: for HSM integration, is Redwood able to do remote attestation against our HSM vendor?
[05:29] Marcus: yes, we can integrate with external HSM attestation APIs - for example AWS Nitro Enclaves or external HSM vendors with attestation flows. we can accept attested public keys and use them in our envelope encryption flow.
[05:40] Priya: about key rotation — we have a policy for weekly key rotation for ephemeral keys and quarterly for master keys. how does Redwood surface rotation events in the audit log?
[05:49] Ravi: rotation events are emitted as part of the audit stream with before/after key IDs (where after is the new wrapping key id). you can configure whether full key IDs are present or truncated to avoid leaking key material. rotation timestamps are included and signed.
[06:02] Samir: on the topic of data residency, we have regulatory requirement to keep all PHI in eu-west-1. can we ensure inference execution and caches never leave that region?
[06:12] Sofia: yes, you can pin model serving pools to a region and enforce a routing policy so requests that originate for eu region only hit eu-hosted pools. KV cache and prefix caches can be pinned regionally as well.
[06:22] Priya: about KV cache security — is cache encrypted at rest and purged on key rotation?
[06:29] Ravi: caches are encrypted at rest with the same envelope keys; on rotation we rotate the data encryption keys and optionally trigger a cache flush depending on your policy. we support lazy-rewrap or full rewrap.
[06:40] (brief crosstalk)
[06:44] David: can we get a demo of the audit log pipeline? seeing event shape helps.
[06:49] Sofia: yes, we prepared a sample event schema. i'll upload after the call. example: event_type: inference.request, fields: request_id, user_id (masked), model, latency_ms, keystore_id, action: decrypt, signed_hash.
[07:01] Priya: will model versions be auditable — we need to tie a user request to a specific model binary/hashing to prove reproducibility.
[07:08] Ravi: every model artifact has a content-addressable hash and we include the model hash in request events. that way you can reproduce inference if you hold the artifact.
[07:16] Marcus: quick pause to recap — so far: airlock pattern with private link or site-to-site, mutual TLS and cert rotation, customer-managed KMS with HSM option, signed audit events with redaction options, regional pinning for data residency, KV cache encryption and rotation semantics.
[07:32] (laughter)
[07:35] Liam: what about the router level — if a request falls back to a lower-cost model variant, is that visible in logs and does it require new egress?
[07:42] Sofia: fallbacks are visible — we log the chosen model id and variant. fallback to a different provider would require explicit peering / allowed egress; by default we don't cross-peering to public endpoints.
[07:52] Priya: procurement question — for private deployment what's the minimum support SLA? we need on-call 24/7 for incidents.
[07:58] Marcus: we have enterprise SLAs available as an add-on. typical private customers take the 24/7 incident support package plus runbook co-authoring.
[08:07] Maya: for SOC 2 audits, will Redwood provide a control matrix and sample evidence?
[08:12] Marcus: yes — we'll provide a SOC 2 bridge packet with relevant logs, configuration snapshots, key rotation history, and RBAC mappings. note: some items are customer-controlled and we can supply templates for evidence collection.
[08:25] (typing)
[08:33] David: edge case — if our VPC egress gateway fails, do you have a fail-open option for latency-sensitive calls? or is fail-closed required by default?
[08:43] Ravi: default is fail-closed for security. we can support a configurable failover lane that routes to a quarantine endpoint or degraded local model instance. it's a policy decision — we'd document in the runbook.
[08:54] Marcus: can i ask about network logging retention — you mentioned write-once, what retention windows are supported?
[09:00] Maya: regulatory requires seven years for certain records.
[09:04] Sofia: we can write logs to your write-once storage or to a third-party archival tier; retention windows are configurable — 90 days, 1 year, 7 years, etc. long-term archiving may be a separate billable add-on.
[09:15] Priya: ok practicalities — what do you need from us to scope the pilot?
[09:20] Marcus: sandbox VPC with the peering info and a sample dataset, KMS key alias, and the list of CI/CD registries and artifact endpoints. we also need your compliance checklist for SOC 2 so we can map evidence.
[09:29] Liam: we'll prepare the VPC and sample artifacts. Samir will set up the egress proxy.
[09:33] Samir: right, we'll do a narrow allow-list and a proxy with mutual TLS.
[09:37] (brief silence)
[09:42] Marcus: great — last bit, on RBAC mapping: we recommend scoping RBAC to groups mapped via SCIM and issuing short-lived tokens for service-to-service calls. any concerns?
[09:52] Priya: sounds good, just ensure the mapping is auditable and we can export role change history.
[09:57] Sofia: we emit role-change events to the audit trail and can surface a history endpoint for compliance exports.
[10:05] Marcus: all right let's wrap. Recap of next steps and action items in chat. we'll aim for the lab run week of feb 2. thanks everyone.
[10:14] (meeting ends)

Shared artifacts: https://redwood.app/arch/hearthwell-airlock-2026, https://redwood.app/soc2/bridge-packet, sample event schema attached in the chat.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional speaker mis-attribution and minor word swaps (e.g., KV cache transcribed as K V cash in one snippet).
